examples.text: Можно заняться спортом.
examples.trans: One can do sports.

examples.text: Вика, понимаешь, я бритву дома забыл.
examples.trans: Vika, you see, I forgot my razor at home.

examples.text: Кажется, закончились у него бритвы. А что за обследование?
examples.trans: It seems he ran out of razors. And what kind of checkup is it?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Макс, твои бабушка и дедушка у меня дома.
examples.trans: Max, your grandmother and grandfather are at my home.

examples.text: Вот твоя водка, такая же горькая и крепкая. Пей!
examples.trans: Here is your vodka, just as bitter and strong. Drink!

examples.text: Вот твой обед, дед.
examples.trans: Here is your lunch, grandpa.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'емья'). Common feminine noun meaning 'family' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На вкус совсем безвкусно.
examples.trans: It tastes completely bland.

examples.text: Ну, за тебя и за твою семью!
examples.trans: Well, to you and to your family!

examples.text: За тебя и твою семью!
examples.trans: To you and your family!
